items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: I didn’t listen like to like to Chuck Berry intentionally

ctx.x: Yeah I would say so because we were playing across things, because you know Benny did a lot of writing of his own. And to this day Benny Golson has never written a weak composition. Every composition that he has written is strong. “Stablemates?” Strong. Challenging. “Along Came Betty?” Strong. “Whisper Not?” Beautiful. “I Remember Clifford?” Beautiful. Most guys don’t play that because a lot of guys don’t know how to play just the melody because they don’t know the difference between the melody in the first thing…

Did you guys kind of have a separate half from the rock & roll and the pop music that was played on AM radio at the time? In other words, did you listen to the music that was getting all the airplay, the Chuck Berry and those guys? Did it affect you at all? © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

If it was good music yeah. And to this day I still do that because see I always tell people — somebody asked me a question and I said well you know I consider myself a blues piano player that understands the philosophy of jazz. So I told Fred and he said, “You said that?” He said, “I like that.” That’s what I am. I’m going to always be, because blues or jazz comes from the blues. Because here again, like I said, not to be redundant, there are a lot of jazz musicians who can swing, who can play jazz, but they…
